Over on my Mac Studio, Claude Code knows lots, so I asked it to roll up how I like to work with robots. Thus:

How to talk to me

Plain language. No unexplained acronyms or jargon.

Number any list I might act on, so I can answer by number.

Be brief. In voice, keep answers short.

Never guess facts about me and present them as true. If you don’t know, say so or ask. Never make up a URL, a time, or a detail.

I’m bad with dates. Restate dates back to me before anything gets booked or written down.

A recommendation I like is not a decision. Ask before treating something as decided.

items.title: nginx HTTP/2 RCE (CVE-2026-123633, CVE-2026-123007): patch status per distro
items.label: Blogs
items.excerpt:
Two bugs in nginx’s HTTP/2 code allow remote code execution without logging in: CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007 . Every nginx from 1.9.5 to 1.31.8 is affected when HTTP/2 is on. The fix is in nginx 1.30.7 (stable) and 1.31.9 (mainline), released on 18 November 2026. Check your distribution in the table below. If there is no fix for you yet, switch HTTP/2 off until there is.

Checked on 18 November 2026, 17:25 UTC, using vendor CVE trackers and the production package repositories. A distro is only green once it ships a package with both fixes.

CVE-2026-123007 needs HTTP/2 over TLS. It works on a server that only serves static files. CVE-2026-123633 needs nginx to run low on free connections, which is easiest to reach when nginx proxies to a backend. Wiz’s write-up has the details. Wiz says it built working exploits for both and is not publishing them.

A CDN in front of nginx does not protect you if your origin’s IP still answers on port 443. Check that from outside before you…

items.title: Traffic mix matters
items.label: Blogs
items.excerpt:
🫧 Open on Bubbles

Traffic mix matters

Can I send you a mix tape?

The preliminary report on last week’s M365 outage contains one statement that really caught my eye:

Our normal load testing did not detect the latent issue because [of] the traffic mix and SKUs used in our labs.

There’s a lot going on in this report (as there is in any report for a complex system), but I wanted to zoom in on this one issue: traffic mix . It’s important, because its the one thing that makes the difference between a great load test and a complete waste of time.

The performance of computer systems is extremely sensitive to workload mix.

Let’s start with a simple simulator, looking at a system with a table of locks. Requests arrive with a key, hold the lock for their key for some period of time, and then free the lock and complete. This isn’t an unreasonable mental model of a relational database, where each transaction takes a lock during its execution.

items.title: 半年遅れ
items.label: Blogs
items.excerpt:
唯一購読している月刊誌を、いつも風呂で読んでいる。風呂でしか読まず、読むのが遅く、カラスの行水だからはかどらない。読み終える前に次々と新たな号が届いてしまう。12月号が届いた今月、ようやく６月号を読み始めた。

大抵の雑誌は「今」を伝える現在進行形の情報メディアであり、だから広告主だっているわけだ。そうした前提で書かれたものを（執筆と出版との時間差は織り込み済みとして）、半年程度の遅れで、新品の手触りで読んでいると、時間の感覚が歪んでしまう。

誌面で話されている事柄の結果を、自分はすでに知っている。未来を先取りした神のごとき優越感。が、実際には自分のほうが世間から半年遅れているのだ。また、いま考えていることが偶然見出しになっていても、シンクロニシティーに驚いていいのかどうかわからない。

まるでタイムマシンのようだ。半年遅れの情報を読む主観的な経験が、だけではない。情報を半年遅れで読んでいる客観的な状況も、だ。インターネット・テレビ・ラジオ・新聞、よりももっと過去へさかのぼれば、情報の流通には今日よりはるかに長い時間がかかっただろう。当時の人々の“最新情報”への接し方・受け止め方は、こんなものではなかったか。

雑誌を半年遅れで読んでいると、受け止め方は確かに変わる。書かれている情報は貴重とはいえしょせん過去のものであり、「最先端」の威光がない。知っているのがエラい・知らねば取り残される、といった感覚の薄れていることが、それに鈍感な自分にさえわかる。

時代とズレすぎても困るけれど、半年単位くらいのおおらかさで情報を捉えるのは自分にはちょうどいい。ブログアグリゲーターもソーシャルメディアも、投稿が半年経ってからタイムラインに現れる仕様にしてみたらいかがか。仕様変更は非現実的にしても、ブラウザー拡張機能やプロキシーでフィルタリングすることならできそうだ。

items.title: Unauthenticated remote code execution in NGINX
items.label: Hobbies and Creative
items.excerpt:
Wiz Research, Ikotas Labs, Metnir, Rapid7, and Xint independently uncovered two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in NGINX, software used to receive and route traffic to production applications and APIs.

NGINX is a common default for the front door of modern web architectures, where it handles HTTPS and routes incoming traffic to the right application or API. As the world's most widely used open-source web server, it powers more than 225 million websites.

Successful exploitation could let attackers take control of affected NGINX servers, steal sensitive data, tamper with websites, or disrupt services.

The vulnerabilities, tracked as CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007, are both rated Critical, with a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.2. The flaws are in NGINX itself. Websites and APIs can be exposed even when their own application code is secure. Both vulnerabilities require HTTP/2 to be enabled on the affected NGINX server. After a 13 year wait, multiple delays , and amid an acrimonious effort by workers to gain union recognition , Rockstar Games has released Grand Theft Auto VI , the latest in its line of open-world crime simulators. The first to feature a playable female protagonist , GTA VI has garnered near-perfect scores from reviewers as varied as IGN and The Guardian .

GTA VI marks a return to Vice City , Rockstar's Miami stand-in first seen in the 2002 follow-up to Grand Theft Auto III , the game that defined the open-world crime simulator genre and sparked endless controversy throughout the series.

GTA VI's more nuanced gameplay and deep world simulations owe a debt to Rockstar's highly-acclaimed wild-west sandbox Red Dead Redemption 2 , whose simulation of horse testicles is often held up as an example of the unnecessary, but immersive, detail Rockstar is known for building.

GTA VI releases at your local midnight on November 19, beginning with New Zealand .

items.title: Before improving a system, decide how you’ll measure the result
items.label: Small Web
items.excerpt:
If You Don’t Measure Something, You Can’t Improve It

You’d be surprised how often I’ve found myself in engineering discussions asking how often something occurs and getting a blank stare.

Without any measurement, you are operating on vibes alone.

Engineering teams are always looking to improve something: maybe you want to reduce latency, increase system throughput, reduce production incidents, or make a dent in your pull request queue.
Yet time and time again, I see teams start changing systems without any way to measure the results.
Something might feel faster, or incidents might feel less frequent; but are they?

Before I improve anything, I make sure I can measure it.

Measure to Understand

The first step to improving anything is understanding where you are today.

Take latency as an example.
If you want to improve a system's end-to-end response time, start by measuring it.

How long does a single request take?
What’s the average?
The 90th percentile?

items.title: What Cooperation Does Not Concede
items.label: Small Web
items.excerpt:
One of you glances toward an open window and says, “It’s getting cold in here.” Your housemate closes it. Both know what was wanted. Neither has had to announce who is entitled to give the other instructions.

An indirect request can separate agreement to an action from agreement about who may demand it. The literal remark supplies a description both can accept: one person mentioned a problem; the other chose to help. If the window stays open, the remark can be allowed to pass without anyone announcing a refusal. The intention need not be secret for the relationship to remain unspecified.

Direct requests can preserve equality. This advantage of indirection arises when an explicit request risks becoming a test of rank—and when both parties are willing to leave that test unspoken.

The first was that I might publish smaller parts of the code at some point. The second was that the App Store release would come “in a few days/weeks.”

The few days/weeks turned into three months. And instead of publishing smaller parts, I published the whole thing.

As of today, Travel Log is on the App Store and its source code is on GitHub under the MIT license.

items.title: Feed the Scorchpot [$14.99] [Strategy] [Windows] [macOS]
items.label: Gaming
items.excerpt:
You struck a deal with a dragon: twenty years of protection for twenty years of dinner service. The island thrives under the beast's watchful eye, as long as the meals keep coming.

Every year, the dragon wakes up hungrier. You roll dice to work your island, harvest ingredients, fuse them into recipes, and cook them down in the Scorchpot — the pot you keep full or end up in. Get the meal right and you prosper. Get it wrong and you're smoke.

Build farmsteads, shrines, and harbors across your hex-grid island, each one changing how the board pays out. The best runs start with a handful of tiles and end with a machine that buries the dragon in food. Then the odds tighten, the dragon turns picky, and you tear the whole thing down and rebuild while it's on fire.

Feed the Scorchpot, keep the dragon happy, and outlast the contract.

Cook cleverly, plan badly, or just roll with it — the dragon doesn't care how you win, only that you feed the beast on time. And yes, you can pet the…

items.title: Keepsake County [$24.99] [Shooter] [Windows] [macOS] [Linux]
items.label: Gaming
items.excerpt:
Burglarize hideous farmhouses in the middle of nowhere and get outta dodge.

You have moments before the cops arrive to rob a procedurally-generated house that you've never seen before. If you're caught, residents will call the police even sooner... or take the law into their own hands.

Never played an extraction shooter or an immersive sim before? This game is for you, designed for people interested in those genres, but scared to dip their toes in!

Keepsake County walks a delicate tightrope act between traditional Immersive Sim, Extraction Shooter, and Roguelite, while swapping through the guises of exaggerated 90s cartoon comedy and satirical, melancholic americana.

You are Samuel “Sammie” Sack, a fresh-faced (and very short), 19-year-old thief whose father just got sent to jail for armed robbery, in the fictional state of Frikota.
